title: Typography and captions
purpose: Lifts title, caption and label styling (position, size, weight, case, colour, backing, chunking) and caption timing against speech.
boundary: The swarm lifts technique and structure only. Never store, transcribe or reuse the source's footage, frames, music, voice or script text. Keyframes and spectrograms are temporary analysis files in a scratch directory and are never copied into the format IR or a variant. On-screen text may be quoted only as a locating note in evidence.note, at most 6 words, and narration is never quoted. Patterns replace content words with slots, e.g. 'FACT {n}' or '{number} {unit} {noun}'. Analysing a public video for technique is fine; republishing its content is not.
inspect: F3 crops of caption, title and label regions enlarged 2x; F9 for text and backing colours; F8 around caption changes.
pitfalls: Naming a specific font from appearance; give a font class instead
Measuring caption sync from a transcription whose own timing error is unknown

methods.measured: A measurement tool produced the value (an evidence.json field or an ffmpeg/ffprobe filter output). Name the tool and the field.
methods.observed: You looked at extracted frames, crops, scopes, spectrograms or waveforms and saw it. Give the timestamps you looked at.
methods.inferred: Reasoned from measured or observed facts, e.g. 'synthetic voice' from flat pitch on a spectrogram. State the reasoning in the note.
methods.assumed: No direct evidence; a default or convention. Use only for gaps the format needs filled, and keep confidence at 0.3 or lower.

pointer_conventions: ir_path is a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into the Video format IR (contract schema video_re_format_ir).
A final '/-' means 'append this answer to the array' (the RFC 6901 end-of-array token), e.g. /motion/transitions/- or /generation_rules/-.
A '*' segment means 'each array element the answer is about'; the answer must say which elements (for example beats with role 'item'). The lifter resolves '*' to concrete indexes.
Paths under free-form objects (typography.title, typography.captions, typography.labels, audio.narration, audio.music, render_binding.mapping) use the snake_case key named in the question.

answer_types.number: {"value": n, "unit": "..."} optionally with "min" and "max"; becomes an IR observed_number
answer_types.ms: {"value": n, "unit": "ms"} optionally with "min"/"max"; signed when an offset (negative = earlier)
answer_types.enum: exactly one of the question's choices (a string)
answer_types.list: array of short strings (technique names or kinds)
answer_types.rule: one procedural generation rule string, at most 400 characters, written in terms of parameters
answer_types.object: a JSON object with the keys the question's how_to_answer names

recipes.F3: Full-resolution crop (add ,scale=iw*2:-1:flags=lanczos to enlarge): ffmpeg -v error -ss T -i "$SRC" -frames:v 1 -vf "crop=W:H:X:Y" "$WORK/crop_T.png"
recipes.F8: Every frame in a short window (animation timing; frame k is at T + k/fps): ffmpeg -v error -ss T -t 0.5 -i "$SRC" -vf "scale=540:-2" "$WORK/step_T_%03d.png"
recipes.F9: Average colour of a region: ffmpeg -v error -ss T -i "$SRC" -frames:v 1 -vf "crop=W:H:X:Y,scale=1:1:flags=area,format=rgb24" -f rawvideo - | od -An -tu1
recipes.A1: Spectrogram image (add highpass=f=3000, before showspectrumpic to isolate clicks and whooshes): ffmpeg -v error -ss T -t D -i "$SRC" -lavfi "showspectrumpic=s=1200x600:legend=1" "$WORK/spec_T.png"

questions.question: Where do captions sit vertically (median y centre as a fraction of frame height)?
questions.how_to_answer: Median y_center_ratio of evidence.text_regions[] entries in the caption role (recurring regions that change with speech); confirm on 3 F1 frames.
questions.challenge: Separate titles and labels from captions before taking the median; report how regions were assigned.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of caption lines on screen at once?
questions.how_to_answer: Inspect F3 crops of the caption area at 6 times; count lines.
questions.challenge: Check the longest caption cards; maximums hide there.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of words on screen in one caption card?
questions.how_to_answer: Word counts of caption cards (evidence.captions[] when burned-in OCR exists, otherwise F3 crops at 6 times); report max and median.
questions.challenge: Word-by-word captions show one word at a time; distinguish card words from highlighted words.

questions.question: What font class do captions use (geometric sans, grotesque sans, condensed sans, rounded sans, serif, slab, handwritten, display)?
questions.why_it_matters: Gives a font class the renderer can map to an open font.
questions.how_to_answer: Enlarged F3 crops: check letter shapes (round 'o' and 'e' for geometric; narrow letters for condensed; serifs).
questions.challenge: Never name a specific commercial font as fact; a named font must be marked inferred.

questions.question: What weight are captions (regular, medium, bold, black)?
questions.how_to_answer: Measure stem width / cap height on enlarged F3 crops and report the ratio. Rough guide (this swarm's convention, not a type standard): about 0.10-0.15 reads as regular, about 0.2 as bold, 0.25 or more as black.
questions.challenge: Outline strokes add apparent weight; measure the fill only.

questions.question: What case do captions use (all caps, sentence case, title case, lower case)?
questions.how_to_answer: F3 crops at 6 times.
questions.challenge: Check at least one caption with a proper noun.

questions.question: What colour is caption text, and what colour marks highlighted or key words?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills caption colour and highlight colour.
questions.how_to_answer: F9 average colour inside thick strokes (3x3 px) of normal and highlighted words.
questions.challenge: Sample three letters for each and report the spread.

questions.question: What backing do captions have (none, stroke, drop shadow, solid box, frosted panel)?
questions.how_to_answer: F3 crops around letters and panel edges over busy and calm backgrounds.
questions.challenge: Compare two frames with different backgrounds to tell a frosted panel from a solid box.

questions.question: If captions have an outline stroke, how thick is it relative to letter height?
questions.how_to_answer: On an enlarged F3 crop, measure the stroke width in px / cap height in px.
questions.challenge: Anti-aliasing adds a pixel; report the measurement method.

questions.question: How tall are caption letters as a fraction of frame height (cap height)?
questions.how_to_answer: Measure the cap height of an upper-case letter in px on an F3 crop / source.height.
questions.challenge: Text bboxes include descenders and padding; use letter measurements.

questions.question: What is the mean offset between caption appearance and the matching spoken word (ms; negative = caption early)?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills caption sync; a common house rule is within 150 ms.
questions.how_to_answer: For 10 caption cards, compare the on-screen appearance time (F8 at caption changes, or text_regions t_s) with the speech onset of the first word (A1 spectrogram or speech_segments).
questions.challenge: Transcribed captions are not on-screen timings; only burned-in text can measure on-screen sync. Report n and spread.

questions.question: Do captions appear before, on, or after the spoken word?
questions.why_it_matters: Summarises sync behaviour for the caption timing rule.
questions.how_to_answer: From 011: 'on' when the mean is within +/-100 ms and the spread is under 150 ms.
questions.challenge: Must agree with the numbers in 011.

questions.question: Are captions shown as phrase cards, word-by-word reveals, or karaoke-style highlighting within a card?
questions.how_to_answer: F8 frame steps across a caption: watch whether words appear one at a time or highlights move.
questions.challenge: Check two cards; mixed behaviour must be reported.

questions.question: How are key words emphasised (colour change, scale pop, weight change, underline, box)?
questions.how_to_answer: Compare emphasised and normal words on F3 crops and F8 steps.
questions.challenge: Each listed method needs one timestamp.

questions.question: How long does a caption card stay on screen (median, min, max)?
questions.how_to_answer: From burned-in caption changes (text_regions in caption area) or evidence.captions[] when they represent the burned-in captions.
questions.challenge: Say which source the timings came from.

questions.question: Are captions on screen during speech pauses, or do they clear when nobody is speaking?
questions.how_to_answer: Check frames inside speech gaps over 0.5 s (speech_segments) for caption text.
questions.challenge: Check at least 4 gaps.

questions.question: How are captions aligned horizontally, and what is their maximum width as a fraction of the frame?
questions.how_to_answer: evidence.text_regions[] bbox x and width for caption regions; report alignment and max width ratio.
questions.challenge: Left-aligned and centred look alike for one-line captions; check multi-line cards.

questions.question: What font class and weight does the title use, and is it the same family as captions?
questions.how_to_answer: Compare enlarged F3 crops of title and captions.
evidence_required: frames: F3 title and caption crops
questions.challenge: Same weight but different family is a common confusion; compare 'a', 'g', 'R'.

questions.question: What colour is title text across title appearances?
questions.how_to_answer: F9 inside title strokes in each title appearance.
questions.challenge: Report the spread over appearances; one sample is not enough.

questions.question: What case and letter spacing does the title use?
questions.how_to_answer: F3 crops; tracking judged from gap between letters relative to stem width.
questions.challenge: Give measured gap/stem values.

questions.question: Where does the title sit when it appears (y centre ratio, alignment), across all title appearances?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills title placement beyond the first frame.
questions.how_to_answer: evidence.text_regions[] for the title role.
questions.challenge: Compare with the hook lens answer for the first frame; differences must be explained.

questions.question: How are item labels styled (font class, weight, colour, size ratio, backing, position)?
questions.how_to_answer: F3 and F9 on labels in 3 items; evidence.text_regions[] for position.
questions.challenge: All fields must be consistent across the 3 items or reported as varying.

questions.question: How large are key numbers compared with caption text (height ratio)?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills the number size ratio for reveals.
questions.how_to_answer: Number glyph height / caption cap height on F3 crops.
questions.challenge: Measure at the number's settled size, not during its entrance animation.

questions.question: What are the minimum text margins from the frame edges (fraction of width and height)?
questions.how_to_answer: Min of bbox distances to each edge over evidence.text_regions[].
questions.challenge: Exclude watermark regions; they are not format text.

questions.question: How often does text overlap faces or the main subject?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a placement constraint or confirms text-over-subject style.
questions.how_to_answer: For 10 frames with text and a subject, count overlaps.
questions.challenge: Report n; do not identify faces.

questions.question: Are emoji or icons used in captions or labels?
questions.how_to_answer: F3 crops of captions and labels.
questions.challenge: Check 6 or more cards.

questions.question: How is punctuation handled in captions (kept, stripped, only question marks)?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a caption text cleaning rule.
questions.how_to_answer: Inspect F3 crops of cards at sentence ends.
questions.challenge: Check at least 3 sentence-final cards.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of characters per caption line, and are lines balanced in length?
questions.how_to_answer: Count characters per line on F3 crops of the 5 longest cards.
questions.challenge: Report counts per card.

questions.question: What is the approximate contrast ratio between caption text and its immediate backing?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets a minimum contrast for generated captions.
questions.how_to_answer: WCAG ratio from F9 samples of text fill and backing (or background next to the stroke).
questions.challenge: Report the worst of 3 samples over different backgrounds.

questions.question: How many distinct text styles appear in the whole video (title, caption, label, number, source line, CTA)?
questions.why_it_matters: Bounds the style count of the type system.
questions.how_to_answer: Group F3 crops of all text roles by font class, weight, colour and size.
questions.challenge: Differences only in size count as one style.

questions.question: Is letter spacing tight, normal or wide in captions?
questions.how_to_answer: Measure the gap between letters relative to stem width on F3 crops and report it; this swarm calls below 0.5 tight and above 1.2 wide (a convention, not a standard).
questions.challenge: Report measured ratios.

questions.question: Do captions stay clear of the bottom 20% and the right-hand 15% of the frame where vertical-video apps often draw controls?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a placement constraint; the exact zones vary by app and must be confirmed per platform.
questions.how_to_answer: Check caption bboxes in evidence.text_regions[] against those bands; read evidence.safe_area.violations for the template used.
questions.challenge: Name the safe-area template the probe used; percentages are a working assumption, not a platform specification.

questions.question: Are captions burned into the picture, supplied as a separate subtitle track, or absent?
questions.why_it_matters: Tells the pipeline which caption source to emit.
questions.how_to_answer: A7 stream list for subtitle streams; F1 frames for burned-in text; evidence.captions[] source as reported by video_re_caption_track.
questions.challenge: evidence.captions[] may come from transcription; it proves speech, not on-screen captions.

questions.question: What caption style parameters should a new video set (font class, colours, highlight, max words, position)?
questions.how_to_answer: Collect answers 001-014 into typed parameters with observed defaults.
questions.challenge: Each parameter needs derived_from.

questions.question: Write the caption chunking and timing rule (max words, break points, minimum hold, sync source).
questions.why_it_matters: Gives the compiler a procedural caption plan.
questions.how_to_answer: From 003, 011, 015 and 028, for example 'cards of at most N words, break at punctuation, hold at least X ms, time from word timestamps, never time-stretch speech'.
questions.challenge: Apply the rule to 3 observed captions; the predicted card breaks should match at least 2.

questions.question: What is the largest share of the frame area covered by text at any moment?
questions.how_to_answer: Max over t of sum(area_ratio) from evidence.text_regions[] grouped by t_s.
questions.challenge: Backing panels may be included in bboxes; state whether they were.
